questions.stem: A 61-year-old man has metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600E mutation. He starts vemurafenib as a single drug, and his lung metastases shrink. Eight weeks later he has two new firm, dome-shaped nodules with a central keratin-filled crater, one on his forearm and one on his cheek. Biopsy of one nodule shows well-differentiated squamous cells with keratin pearls. DNA from this new lesion shows an HRAS mutation and normal (wild-type) BRAF. Which mechanism best explains the new lesions?
choices: Direct alkylation of keratinocyte DNA by the drug and its metabolites
Paradoxical activation of RAF-MEK-ERK signaling in keratinocytes
Transformation of circulating melanoma cells into squamous cells
Loss of immune surveillance because the drug depletes CD8+ T cells
Loss of PTCH1 function that switches on Hedgehog signaling in skin
questions.explanation: BRAF inhibitors block the mutant BRAF protein, but in cells with **wild-type BRAF** and an active upstream **RAS** (often an *HRAS* mutation from sun damage), the drug binds one RAF partner of a dimer and **transactivates** the other (CRAF). The result is **paradoxical MAPK (ERK) activation**, which drives **keratoacanthomas** and well-differentiated **squamous cell carcinomas**; adding a MEK inhibitor reduces this effect. Loss of immune surveillance is the most tempting choice because it explains SCC in transplant recipients, but vemurafenib does not deplete T cells, and the lesion's own RAS mutation points to a signaling cause.
questions.explanation_pt: Os inibidores de BRAF bloqueiam a proteína BRAF mutada, mas em células com **BRAF selvagem** e **RAS** ativo a montante (muitas vezes uma mutação de *HRAS* causada por dano solar), o fármaco se liga a um parceiro RAF de um dímero e **transativa** o outro (CRAF). O resultado é a **ativação paradoxal da via MAPK (ERK)**, que leva a **ceratoacantomas** e **carcinomas espinocelulares** bem diferenciados; associar um inibidor de MEK reduz esse efeito. A perda da vigilância imunológica é a opção mais tentadora porque explica o CEC em transplantados, mas o vemurafenibe não causa depleção de linfócitos T, e a mutação de RAS na própria lesão aponta para uma causa de sinalização.

questions.stem: A 69-year-old man who worked outdoors for 40 years has many rough, pink, scaly papules on his bald scalp and the backs of his hands. They feel like sandpaper. Biopsy of one papule shows atypical keratinocytes in the lower part of the epidermis with overlying parakeratosis; the dermis is not invaded. He is given a cream to treat the whole sun-damaged area. The drug works mainly without killing cells directly; it makes local dendritic cells and macrophages release interferon-α and other cytokines, and the treated skin becomes red and crusted. Which molecule is the direct target of this drug?
questions.explanation: The lesions are **actinic keratoses**, premalignant lesions that can progress to **squamous cell carcinoma**. The cream is **imiquimod**, a **TLR7 agonist** that triggers innate immune cells to release **interferon-α**, TNF and IL-12, which leads to an immune attack on atypical keratinocytes. Thymidylate synthase is the most tempting choice because topical **5-fluorouracil** is also used for actinic keratoses, but 5-FU *inhibits* that enzyme and kills dividing cells directly, not through an immune response.
questions.explanation_pt: As lesões são **ceratoses actínicas**, lesões pré-malignas que podem evoluir para **carcinoma espinocelular**. O creme é o **imiquimode**, um **agonista do TLR7** que faz as células da imunidade inata liberarem **interferon-α**, TNF e IL-12, o que leva a um ataque imune contra os queratinócitos atípicos. A timidilato sintase é a opção mais tentadora porque a **5-fluoruracila** tópica também é usado na ceratose actínica, mas a 5-FU *inibe* essa enzima e mata diretamente as células em divisão, sem depender de resposta imune.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old Black woman notices a dark stripe in the nail of her right great toe. Over the past year it has become wider. She does not remember any injury. Exam shows a 5-mm-wide brown-black band that runs the length of the nail, with uneven color and blurred edges. The pigment extends onto the skin of the proximal nail fold. The rest of her skin has no unusual moles, and she rarely gets sunburned. Which diagnosis is most likely?
questions.explanation: A widening, irregular pigmented nail band with pigment spreading onto the nail fold (**Hutchinson nail sign**) suggests **acral lentiginous melanoma**, the most common melanoma subtype in people with darker skin; it affects the palms, soles and nail beds and is **not linked to UV exposure**. A subungual hematoma is the most tempting choice, but it usually follows trauma, grows out with the nail and does not stain the skin of the nail fold. Lentigo maligna melanoma arises on chronically sun-damaged facial skin of older adults.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma faixa pigmentada ungueal irregular que se alarga, com pigmento que se estende para a dobra ungueal (**sinal de Hutchinson ungueal**), sugere **melanoma lentiginoso acral**, o subtipo de melanoma mais comum em pessoas de pele mais escura; acomete palmas, plantas e leito ungueal e **não tem relação com a exposição UV**. O hematoma subungueal é a opção mais tentadora, mas costuma seguir um trauma, migra com o crescimento da unha e não pigmenta a pele da dobra ungueal. O melanoma lentigo maligno surge na pele facial com dano solar crônico de idosos.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man was badly burned on his right leg in a house fire 30 years ago. The area healed with a thick scar that has broken down and reopened many times. Over the past 4 months, an ulcer in the scar has grown larger. Its edges are now hard, raised and turned outward, and it bleeds easily and smells bad. A firm, painless lymph node is felt in the right groin. Biopsy of the ulcer edge is most likely to show which finding?
choices: Nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading
Atypical melanocytes that stain for HMB-45
Small round blue cells with perinuclear CK20 dots
Spindle cells that form slit-like vascular spaces
Atypical squamous cells with keratin pearls
questions.explanation: An ulcer that grows in an old **burn scar** or other chronic wound is a **Marjolin ulcer**, which is usually a **squamous cell carcinoma**: invasive atypical squamous cells with **keratin pearls**. These tumors behave aggressively and can spread to regional **lymph nodes**, as in this patient. Basal cell carcinoma is the most tempting choice because it is the most common skin cancer, but it arises far less often in scars and almost never metastasizes.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma úlcera que cresce em uma antiga **cicatriz de queimadura** ou outra ferida crônica é uma **úlcera de Marjolin**, que geralmente é um **carcinoma espinocelular**: células escamosas atípicas invasivas com **pérolas córneas**. Esses tumores são agressivos e podem se disseminar para **linfonodos** regionais, como neste paciente. O carcinoma basocelular é a opção mais tentadora por ser o câncer de pele mais comum, mas surge em cicatrizes com muito menos frequência e quase nunca dá metástase.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman develops an infection of her abdominal surgical wound. The wound is opened, cleaned and left open to heal by secondary intention. At first the open area measures 6 cm × 4 cm. Over the next 3 weeks the base fills with beefy red, granular tissue, and the open area shrinks to about 3 cm × 2 cm before new epithelium covers it. Which cell is mainly responsible for pulling the wound edges together?
questions.explanation: The open area fell from 24 cm² to about 6 cm², a reduction of about three quarters, because of **wound contraction**. This is done by **myofibroblasts**: fibroblasts that, under **TGF-β**, gain **α-smooth muscle actin** and pull on the granulation tissue and surrounding matrix. Ordinary fibroblasts are the most tempting choice because they lay down the **type III collagen** that fills the wound, but collagen deposition fills the defect rather than drawing its edges together; keratinocytes only cover the surface.
questions.explanation_pt: A área aberta caiu de 24 cm² para cerca de 6 cm², uma redução de cerca de três quartos, por causa da **contração da ferida**. Ela é feita pelos **miofibroblastos**: fibroblastos que, sob ação do **TGF-β**, passam a expressar **actina de músculo liso α** e tracionam o tecido de granulação e a matriz ao redor. Os fibroblastos comuns são a opção mais tentadora porque depositam o **colágeno tipo III** que preenche a ferida, mas a deposição de colágeno preenche o defeito em vez de aproximar suas bordas; os queratinócitos apenas recobrem a superfície.

questions.stem: A 3-year-old boy has had fever and irritability for 1 day. His skin became red and very tender, first around his mouth and in the skin folds. Today large sheets of skin on his trunk peel off with gentle rubbing, leaving moist red areas. There are crusts around the mouth, but the inside of the mouth and the eyes are normal. Results: temperature 38.6°C (101.5°F); pulse 128/min; blood pressure 94/58 mm Hg; leukocyte count 13,500/mm3; blood culture: no growth at 48 hours. A frozen section of peeled skin shows a split high in the epidermis, in the granular layer, with no dead keratinocytes. Which protein is the target of the toxin responsible for this condition?
questions.explanation: This is **staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome**: *S. aureus* growing at a small site (often around the nose or mouth) releases **exfoliative toxins** that spread through the blood and cleave **desmoglein 1**, splitting the epidermis in the **granular layer**. Blood cultures are often negative because the toxin, not the bacterium, spreads, and the mucosa is spared because mucosal epithelium relies mostly on desmoglein 3. Desmoglein 3 is the most tempting choice, but autoantibodies against it cause **pemphigus vulgaris**, with a deeper suprabasal split and painful oral erosions.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se da **síndrome da pele escaldada estafilocócica**: o *S. aureus* que cresce em um pequeno foco (muitas vezes perto do nariz ou da boca) libera **toxinas esfoliativas** que circulam pelo sangue e clivam a **desmogleína 1**, separando a epiderme na **camada granulosa**. As hemoculturas costumam ser negativas porque quem se dissemina é a toxina, e não a bactéria, e as mucosas são poupadas porque o epitélio mucoso depende principalmente da desmogleína 3. A desmogleína 3 é a opção mais tentadora, mas autoanticorpos contra ela causam o **pênfigo vulgar**, com clivagem suprabasal mais profunda e erosões orais dolorosas.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 1 hour after his clothes caught fire. Results: temperature 36.9°C (98.4°F); pulse 118/min; blood pressure 104/66 mm Hg; respirations 22/min; oxygen saturation 97% on room air. On the right forearm the skin is pink, moist and blistered, and it is very painful to light touch. On the right thigh there is a dry, white, leathery area that does not blanch with pressure, and he does not feel a pinprick there. Which best explains the lack of pain in the thigh area?
choices: Release of endorphins from the stress of the injury
Swelling that compresses the main nerve of the limb
Injury limited to the outer layers of the epidermis
Loss of the epidermis with intact dermal nerve endings
Destruction of the whole dermis and its nerve endings
questions.explanation: The thigh has a **full-thickness burn**: the epidermis and the **whole dermis** are destroyed, including its sensory nerve endings, so the area is dry, white or leathery and **painless**. With no surviving hair follicles or sweat glands, it can heal only from the edges and usually needs **grafting**. Loss of the epidermis with intact dermal nerves is the most tempting choice, but that describes the **partial-thickness** burn on the forearm, which blisters and is very painful because exposed nerve endings are still alive.
questions.explanation_pt: A coxa tem uma **queimadura de espessura total**: a epiderme e **toda a derme** foram destruídas, incluindo as terminações nervosas sensitivas, por isso a área é seca, branca ou com aspecto de couro e **indolor**. Sem folículos pilosos ou glândulas sudoríparas restantes, ela só cicatriza a partir das bordas e geralmente precisa de **enxerto**. A perda da epiderme com nervos dérmicos intactos é a opção mais tentadora, mas descreve a queimadura de **espessura parcial** do antebraço, que forma bolhas e é muito dolorosa porque as terminações nervosas expostas continuam vivas.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman has had fever, chills and a painful red rash on her left cheek for 1 day. Temperature is 38.9°C (102°F) and pulse is 104/min. The left cheek has a bright red, shiny, warm plaque that is raised above the nearby skin. Its edge is sharp, and you can feel the step at the border with a fingertip. There is no pus, blister or fluctuance. A small crack in the skin is seen at the left nostril. Which organism most likely caused this infection?
questions.explanation: A shiny, raised plaque with a **sharp, palpable border** and fever is **erysipelas**, an infection of the **upper dermis and superficial lymphatics**; the lymphatic involvement gives the raised, well-defined edge. It is caused mainly by **group A *Streptococcus*** (*S. pyogenes*), which entered through the crack at the nostril. *S. aureus* is the most tempting choice, but it is typical of purulent infections such as abscesses and furuncles, and of cellulitis with pus, while erysipelas is nonpurulent and streptococcal.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma placa brilhante e elevada, com **borda nítida e palpável**, associada a febre, é **erisipela**, infecção da **derme superior e dos linfáticos superficiais**; o acometimento linfático explica a borda elevada e bem delimitada. É causada principalmente pelo ***Streptococcus* do grupo A** (*S. pyogenes*), que entrou pela fissura na narina. O *S. aureus* é a opção mais tentadora, mas é típico de infecções purulentas, como abscessos e furúnculos, e de celulite com pus, enquanto a erisipela é não purulenta e estreptocócica.
